title: Grade 11 Mathematics — Mixed Review: Probability & Statistics
description: Probability, measures of dispersion, mean deviation, variance
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The probability of an event A, P(A), satisfies:
questions.explanation: Probability axioms: 0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1. P(impossible event) = 0. P(certain event) = 1. P(A) + P(A') = 1 (complementary events).

questions.question: Addition rule for probability: P(A∪B) = ?
questions.explanation: P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A∩B). For mutually exclusive events (A∩B = ∅): P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) (since P(A∩B) = 0).

questions.question: A fair die is thrown. P(getting a prime number) is:
questions.explanation: Prime numbers on a die: 2, 3, 5 (three primes out of six equally likely outcomes). P = 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.question: The variance of a data set is the average of the:
questions.explanation: Variance σ² = Σ(xᵢ − x̄)²/n. Standard deviation σ = √(Variance). Variance penalises large deviations more (squaring). Mean deviation uses absolute values: Σ|xᵢ − x̄|/n.

questions.question: Two cards are drawn at random (without replacement) from a deck of 52. P(both are kings) is:
questions.explanation: P(first king) = 4/52. P(second king | first king) = 3/51 (one fewer king and one fewer card). P(both kings) = 4/52 × 3/51 = 12/2652 = 1/221.

questions.question: For the data 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9, the mean is:
The standard deviation of the data: 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9 is: (Mean = 5)
questions.explanation: Deviations from mean: −3,−1,−1,−1,0,0,2,4. Squared: 9,1,1,1,0,0,4,16. Sum = 32. Variance = 32/8 = 4. SD = √4 = 2.

questions.question: If A and B are independent events, P(A∩B) = ?
questions.explanation: For independent events: P(A∩B) = P(A) × P(B). Events A and B are independent if the occurrence of one does not affect the probability of the other.

Coefficient of variation (CV) is used to compare variability and equals:
questions.explanation: CV = (σ/x̄) × 100%. It expresses standard deviation as a percentage of the mean. Lower CV = more consistent data. Useful for comparing variability of datasets with different units or means.

questions.question: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed using digits 1-5 without repetition?
The number of ways to choose 3 books from 8 distinct books (order doesn't matter) is:
The range of the data 3, 7, 2, 9, 4, 11, 1 is:
questions.explanation: Range = Maximum − Minimum = 11 − 1 = 10. Range is the simplest measure of dispersion.

questions.question: P(A') where A' is the complement of A, equals:
questions.explanation: Complement Rule: P(A') = 1 − P(A). P(A) + P(A') = 1. Useful when it is easier to find the probability of the complement: P(at least one) = 1 − P(none).
